title: Dead Mount Death Play
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A feared necromancer, the Corpse God, is cornered by a legendary hero and escapes through reincarnation magic into the body of Polka Shinoyama, a boy in modern Tokyo who had just been targeted by an assassin, Misaki. Hoping for a quiet life, he is drawn into the city's underworld of assassins, gangs, police and the supernatural (Yen Press blurb; ANN Fall 2018 Manga Guide).
life_message: People are not what their reputations say: a feared 'villain' can be kinder than the 'heroes', and judging others by labels is a mistake.

content.note: Assassins, murders and serial killers (MU; AniList Assassins, Gangs); ANN notes Polka kills or hurts many adults.
Necromancy, zombies, ghosts and undead (AniList, MU); ANN describes horror elements.
ANN reviewers note 'random lesbian sex scenes', panty shots and fan service; AniList Nudity (56); MU Nudity, LGBT Scenes.
MU Psychological Trauma; ANN notes the original Polka was sold by his parents.
Contract killing and underworld dealings normalized in the setting (MU Underworld Society).

dominant: Inverted hero-villain roles; occult power used pragmatically; acceptance of outsiders

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Disputes settled by assassins and gangs, not courts (AniList Assassins, Gangs; MU Underworld Society).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Polka seeks a quiet life outside both worlds' authorities (ANN).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Polka's original parents sold him; new bonds are chosen (ANN; MU Important Non-Romantic Relationship/s).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Lead treats people without prejudice regardless of rank (ANN).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Magic treated as a practical tool in a modern city, not as faith.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Hiding and staying alive in a violent underworld drive the plot (Yen Press blurb).

folkways.japan: Set in Shinjuku's underworld, it draws on Japanese urban-legend and yakuza fiction traditions (MU Yakuza/s).

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewers say its theme on the assumptions people make about others comes through characters; none call it preachy.

personified.ideology: Feared necromancer who wants a quiet life and judges no one

delivery.note: The story inverts hero and villain roles, and one reviewer suggests the 'hero' may be the true villain, so the righteous crusader is treated with suspicion.

winners_losers: The reincarnated necromancer survives and wins allies; assassins and criminals who target him lose. Sympathy goes to the misjudged outsider over the 'heroic' order.
